resumen: The same curl with the palms facing each other. It changes the split between the biceps and the muscles underneath.
ejecucion: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing inwards.
Curl up without rotating the wrist: the palm still faces in at the top.
The upper arm stays against your side.
Lower slowly until the elbow is straight.
It usually allows a little more weight than the supinated curl; still no swinging.
matices: The usual claim is that the hammer curl works the brachioradialis more, and the cited study measures the opposite: on the way up, the brachioradialis was 6 % MORE excited with the supinated grip. What the neutral grip does raise is the share taken by the brachialis, which sits under the biceps and cannot be seen.
